answer: The ledger assigns each agent a unique provenance seed generated by an orchard of verifiable randomness beacons; the seed is cryptographically bound to a zephyr‑rate proof‑of‑work that must be posted on a blockchain ledge before any message is accepted. When an identity tries to clone the seed, it must repeat the proof‑of‑work and also lock a stake equal to 10 tokens per replica, otherwise the network rejects the duplicate. Thus a Sybil attacker pays 10 tokens and the computational cost of a full proof‑of‑work for every fake identity.
